info.name: interceptor
info.description:
interceptor endpoints, called through the LiteLLM pass-through registered in ai/litellm/litellm_config.yaml (`pass_through_endpoints` → `/v1/interceptor` → `http://interceptor:8080`, `include_subpath: true`, methods GET/POST/DELETE, `forward_headers: true` — so `multipart/form-data` uploads for /profiles/{name}/refresh forward correctly). Every request is authenticated with a Bearer token from a LiteLLM virtual key. Set the collection variables `litellm` (e.g. http://localhost:4001) and `virtual master key` (an sk-… key issued from the LiteLLM Admin UI → Virtual Keys) — every request inherits them via collection-level auth. See ai/interceptor/INTERCEPTOR.md for the full endpoint reference and ai/litellm/LITELLM.md for issuing virtual keys.

Reaching the service: the container has NO `ports:` mapping (INTERCEPTOR.md § Reaching the service). Port 8080 is reachable only from inside `ai_shared`. Options: (1) another `ai_shared` container via `http://interceptor:8080/...`, (2) your host via the LiteLLM pass-through `{{litellm}}/v1/interceptor/...` (what this collection uses), (3) `docker exec interceptor curl ...`. `http://localhost:8080` from the host does NOT reach the container — if something answers there it's a separate bare-metal `python app.py` run against the host's `/data/profiles` (used during profile capture with a visible display).

MCP: LiteLLM ALSO advertises the interceptor as an MCP server via `mcp_servers.interceptor` (url `http://interceptor:8080/mcp`) — models see the five tools (capture_url, screenshot_url, list_profiles, list_jobs, get_job) through that path. The MCP requests below are useful for debugging the transport directly.

Screenshots: POST /screenshot (and the `screenshot` block on POST /capture) return an image of the rendered page as base64 inside the JSON; the MCP tools deliver it as an ImageContent block instead. See INTERCEPTOR.md § Screenshots.

Actions: POST /capture also takes `page_script` / `actions` / `stop_when_matched` to fill inputs and click buttons (through shadow DOM) so the page fires the request you want — see `POST /capture (actions)` and INTERCEPTOR.md § Page scripts and actions.

Viewing screenshots: a collection-level post-response script renders `screenshot.data_base64` from POST /capture and POST /screenshot — open the **Visualize** tab in the response pane after sending. The header line shows `page_url`, i.e. where the tab actually was when the image was taken (the end of the capture window).

exec: // Renders the screenshot from POST /capture and POST /screenshot in the
// Visualize tab of the response pane. A no-op for every other response
// (MCP results carry the image as an ImageContent block, not base64 here).
try { body = pm.response.json(); } catch (e) { /* not JSON */ }
{ url: s.page_url, w: s.width, h: s.height, fmt: s.format, kb: Math.round(s.bytes / 1024),

variable.description: LiteLLM base URL. Localhost publish is 4001 (PORT_LITELLM); on ai_shared it's http://litellm:4000; behind cloudflared it's https://your-litellm-host.

LiteLLM virtual key (Admin UI → Virtual Keys, or /key/generate API). The pass-through runs with `auth: true`, so a non-admin virtual key needs `/v1/interceptor` in its (or its team's) `metadata.allowed_passthrough_routes` — set under `metadata`, by a proxy admin, because the top-level field is Enterprise-only; the master key works without it. Otherwise 403. See ai/litellm/LITELLM.md § Pass-through auth. Sent as `Authorization: Bearer {{virtual master key}}` by the collection-level auth.

Named Chrome profile. Must match `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}` (profiles.py:_NAME_RE). Used by GET /profiles/{name}, POST /profiles/{name}/refresh, DELETE /profiles/{name}. Discover valid values via GET /profiles.

12-char hex job_id returned by POST /capture (or listed by GET /jobs). Fill in to run GET /jobs/{job_id} and POST /jobs/{job_id}/cancel. Completed captures are NOT retained — the id is only valid while the capture is in flight.

MCP transport session id — paste the `mcp-session-id` response header value returned by the `MCP — initialize` request. Subsequent MCP calls need it. This is FastMCP's HTTP-transport session cookie, unrelated to any interceptor job_id.

request.description: Liveness check. Returns {"status": "ok"} whenever the FastAPI process is up. No dependency checks — this endpoint does not verify Chrome, the profiles volume, or the port pool. Errors: none from the app itself; a network-level failure means the container isn't running or isn't reachable on ai_shared. See INTERCEPTOR.md § Bring it up.

List every named Chrome profile currently on disk under `INTERCEPTOR_PROFILES_ROOT` (default /data/profiles, backed by the `interceptor_data` volume). Returns {root, profiles: [{name, path, present, size_bytes, sentinel_present, login_keys, login_origins}, ...]}. `login_keys` are the credential reference names the profile's `login_actions` may use (`${username}`, `${password}`, …) and `login_origins` the origins they may be typed into — both read from INTERCEPTOR_LOGINS_DIR/<name>.json, both [] when the profile has no logins file, and the values themselves are NEVER returned; `login_error` is added when the file is unusable (INTERCEPTOR.md § Login actions). Directories whose names fail the `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}` validator are silently skipped (profiles.py:list_profiles). `sentinel_present: true` means `session_ok` exists at the profile root — required for headless launch. See INTERCEPTOR.md § Endpoints and § Sanity check before uploading. Errors: none — returns an empty list if the root dir is missing.

Return one profile's status: {name, path, present, size_bytes, sentinel_present} when the directory exists, or {name, path, present: false, size_bytes: 0} when it doesn't — either way plus `login_keys` / `login_origins` (and `login_error` if its logins file is unusable; never a credential value, see GET /profiles) (a missing profile is a 200, not a 404 — see profiles.py:profile_info). Use `sentinel_present` + `size_bytes` to distinguish the container's `/data/profiles` from a bare-metal instance's (both report the same `root`; see INTERCEPTOR.md § Reaching the service).

Errors: 400 if the name fails `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}` (InvalidProfileNameError → HTTPException in app.py:profiles_get).

formdata.description: Required. A .tgz/.tar.gz of a captured Chrome --user-data-dir. The endpoint uses tarfile.open(mode='r:*') so gzip/bzip2/xz auto-detect. Field name MUST be exactly `archive` — any other name returns 422 with no unpack performed. Archive the CONTENTS of the profile dir (`tar czf x.tgz -C <profile_dir> .`), not the dir itself.

request.description:
Upload a .tgz of a captured Chrome profile. WIPES any existing `PROFILES_ROOT/{name}` FIRST (unconditional `shutil.rmtree`), then extracts the archive with `filter='data'` (refuses `..` / absolute paths / device files), then writes a `session_ok` sentinel so the next /capture boots straight to headless. Returns {unpacked: true, name, path, present, size_bytes, sentinel_present}.

Do NOT refresh while a capture is in flight against that profile (unpack ignores the per-profile lock — INTERCEPTOR.md § Refreshing a profile). Check GET /jobs first.

Errors: 400 if name fails the validator, 400 if unpack fails (`failed to unpack profile: ...`) — note the profile dir is already wiped before validation of the archive, so a corrupt or wrong-format upload destroys the working profile. See INTERCEPTOR.md § Refreshing a profile and § Cookie encryption and portability (v11 cookies won't decrypt in the container — re-capture with the launcher's `--password-store=basic` pinning in effect).

Wipe a named profile from disk. Idempotent — returns {name, deleted: true} if the dir existed, {name, deleted: false} if it didn't (profiles.py:delete_profile). Does NOT check the per-profile lock — do not delete while a capture is in flight against that profile.

Errors: 400 if name fails `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}`.

body.raw:
{
  "url": "https://example.com/dashboard",
  "url_patterns": ["example\\.com/api/v1/items", "example\\.com/api/v1/user"],
  "profile": "{{profileName}}",
  "capture_window_seconds": 20,
  "keep_open": false,
  "login_timeout": 300,
  "max_matches_per_pattern": null,
  "debug_logging": false,
  "login_url_patterns": ["login", "signin", "/auth"],
  "screenshot": null,
  "page_script": null,
  "actions": [],
  "actions_ready_timeout_seconds": null,
  "stop_when_matched": false,
  "login_actions": [],
  "login_actions_timeout_seconds": null
}

request.description:
Run one capture. Launches Chrome headless under the named profile, navigates to `url`, and returns every JSON XHR/fetch body whose URL matches any of `url_patterns` (re.search — first-matching-pattern wins). `capture_window_seconds` is a HARD wall (1..600, default 20); Chrome quits when it elapses regardless of state. Must exceed `login_timeout` for a session-refresh to have a chance to resolve.

`login_url_patterns` are re.search-matched against the tab URL AFTER navigation to detect a login-wall redirect. Supplying the field REPLACES the defaults (`["login", "signin", "/auth"]`), does not merge — empty list disables detection. They're full regexes, so `^https?://roofix\.io/?$` distinguishes the logged-out root from in-app URLs.

`keep_open: true` leaves Chrome + port + profile-lock held after the window closes; reclaim by POST /jobs/{id}/cancel or restart the container. Operator-only (not on MCP). `debug_logging: true` prepends `const DEBUG_LOGGING = true;` to interceptor.js so traces appear in the browser console (operator-only).

`screenshot` (optional, default null): set to {format: 'jpeg'|'png'|'webp', quality: 1-100, full_page: bool, scale: 0<s<=2, max_height: 100-16384} — all keys optional — to also capture an image of the page at the end of the window, just before Chrome quits. With `screenshot` set, `url_patterns` may be `[]` (screenshot-only navigation); without it an empty `url_patterns` is a 422.

`page_script`, `actions`, `actions_ready_timeout_seconds`, `stop_when_matched` (all optional; defaults = a plain capture, unchanged behaviour): drive the page so it fires the request you want — see the `POST /capture (actions)` request in this collection and INTERCEPTOR.md § Page scripts and actions.

`login_actions`, `login_actions_timeout_seconds` (optional; default = no automatic login): steps that sign in only if the tab hits a login wall, with `${key}` credential references — see the `POST /capture (login actions)` request and INTERCEPTOR.md § Login actions.

Returns CaptureResponse: {job_id, url, status, login_wall, error, matches (pattern → [{url, body}]), captured_urls (every JSON XHR/fetch seen — use to reverse-engineer regexes), screenshot ({format, mime_type, width, height, full_page, bytes, page_url, data_base64} or null), screenshot_error (set when a requested screenshot failed — the captures are still valid), actions_report (null unless page_script/actions were sent), login_actions_report (same shape; null unless login_actions were sent AND a login wall was hit), ended_early (true only when stop_when_matched closed the window early)}. `login_wall: true` may mean either an expired session OR a v11-cookie-encryption mismatch (INTERCEPTOR.md § Cookie encryption and portability).

Errors: 400 if profile name fails validator, 400 for invalid `url_pattern` or `login_url_pattern` regex (checked before consuming a port), 400 `invalid action: …` for an action the library rejects (e.g. unknown `press` key), 422 if `url_patterns` is empty and no `screenshot` requested, 422 if `stop_when_matched` is set with no `url_patterns`, 422 for a malformed action (unknown `type`, missing field), 400 for a login_actions problem (no logins file for the profile, unknown `${key}`, `${` outside a fill value, missing/empty `allowed_origins`), 422 for `login_actions` with an `evaluate` step or with empty `login_url_patterns`, 429 when the port pool is exhausted (`INTERCEPTOR_MAX_CONCURRENT` slots taken — retry later), 500 if Chrome can't be found (`BrowserNotFoundError`). See INTERCEPTOR.md § POST /capture, § Screenshots and § Concurrency.

body.raw:
{
  "url": "https://support.enphase.com/feoc-compliance/",
  "url_patterns": ["webruntime/api/apex/execute"],
  "profile": "{{profileName}}",
  "capture_window_seconds": 60,
  "login_timeout": 30,
  "login_url_patterns": ["login", "signin", "/auth", "sso\\.enphaseenergy\\.com"],
  "stop_when_matched": true,
  "actions_ready_timeout_seconds": 60,
  "page_script": null,
  "actions": [
    {"type": "fill", "selector": "textarea[placeholder='Serial number']", "value": "532614044013"},
    {"type": "evaluate", "script": "(() => { window.__ciN0 = (window._capturedResponses || []).length; return window.__ciN0; })()"},
    {"type": "click", "selector": "button[type=submit]", "text": "Submit"},
    {"type": "evaluate", "script": "(async () => { const until = Date.now() + 30000; while (Date.now() < until) { const c = (window._capturedResponses || []).slice(window.__ciN0 || 0).filter(x => /webruntime\\/api\\/apex\\/execute/.test(x.url)); if (c.length) return {new_apex_responses: c.length}; await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 250)); } throw new Error('no new apex/execute response within 30s of Submit'); })()", "timeout_s": 35},
    {"type": "wait", "seconds": 2}
  ],
  "screenshot": {"format": "jpeg", "scale": 0.5}
}

request.description:
Same endpoint as POST /capture, driving the page first: for pages that only fire the request you want after someone fills a form and clicks a button. The page's OWN code sends the request (so CSRF-signed APIs such as Salesforce LWR's `webruntime/api/apex/execute` work — a hand-written fetch() from page_script gets 401), and the response arrives in `matches` through the normal capture path. The body is the verified Enphase FEOC serial lookup (2026-10-02); for another site, discover the selectors first with a `page_script` (INTERCEPTOR.md § Worked example). The result is the match whose `returnValue` is a JSON string of an array, e.g. `[{"sn":"532614044013","feoc":"Yes","sku":"IQ8HC-72-M-DOM-US",...}]`.

Order: Chrome launches → readiness gate (tab off about:blank, not on a `login_url_patterns` URL, document.readyState complete, interceptor.js hook installed; up to `actions_ready_timeout_seconds`, default capture_window_seconds) → `page_script` (an EXPRESSION — use an async IIFE for several statements; its value comes back as actions_report.page_script.value) → each action in order, stopping at the first failure (the rest are reported `skipped`).

Step types: `wait_for` {selector, text?, state?: visible|attached, timeout_s?}; `fill` {selector, value, text?, clear?: true, timeout_s?} — focuses the real <input>/<textarea> (descending from a component host such as lightning-input into its shadow root), types with trusted Input.insertText, fires change, blurs; `click` {selector, text?, method?: mouse|js, timeout_s?} — trusted mouse press/release at the element's centre; `press` {key, selector?, text?, timeout_s?} — Enter/Tab/Escape/Backspace/Delete/Space/arrows/Home/End/PageUp/PageDown or one character; `select` {selector, value, text?, timeout_s?} — native <select> only; `wait` {seconds}; `evaluate` {script, timeout_s?}. `timeout_s` defaults to 15. Selectors are CSS matched in the document and inside every open shadow root, each tree separately (a descendant combinator never crosses a shadow boundary — `lightning-input input` matches nothing; use `lightning-input` or `input[name=…]`); `text` filters by visible text / value / aria-label / placeholder / title (substring, or /regex/flags); the first visible match wins.

`stop_when_matched: true` ends the window once every url_patterns bucket has a match AND the actions have finished — the page makes three Apex calls on load (same URL), so the two `evaluate` steps hold the window open: the first records how many responses interceptor.js has captured, the second waits for a new Apex one after Submit; the trailing `wait` lets it reach the service before the window closes. The screenshot (if requested) and cleanup still run.

Response: the usual CaptureResponse plus `actions_report` {page_script: ActionResult|null, actions: [{index, type, ok, elapsed_ms, error, value}], aborted_reason: null | 'not ready: …' | 'cancelled' | 'actions[i] (type) failed: …' | 'capture window ended before actions finished'} and `ended_early`. GET /jobs shows phase `actions` and metadata.actions_done / actions_total while the steps run.

Errors: as POST /capture — 422 for an unknown action `type` or a missing field, 400 `invalid action: …` for an unknown press key, 422 when `stop_when_matched` has no url_patterns — all before a port is taken. See INTERCEPTOR.md § Page scripts and actions.

  "page_script": null,

    {"type": "fill", "selector": "textarea[placeholder='Serial number']", "value": "532614044013"},
    {"type": "evaluate", "script": "(() => { window.__ciN0 = (window._capturedResponses || []).length; return window.__ciN0; })()"},
    {"type": "click", "selector": "button[type=submit]", "text": "Submit"},
    {"type": "evaluate", "script": "(async () => { const until = Date.now() + 30000; while (Date.now() < until) { const c = (window._capturedResponses || []).slice(window.__ciN0 || 0).filter(x => /webruntime\\/api\\/apex\\/execute/.test(x.url)); if (c.length) return {new_apex_responses: c.length}; await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 250)); } throw new Error('no new apex/execute response within 30s of Submit'); })()", "timeout_s": 35},
    {"type": "wait", "seconds": 2}
  ],

}

request.description:
Same endpoint as POST /capture (actions), plus automatic login: the verified Enphase FEOC serial lookup with `login_actions` that sign the profile back in when its SSO session has expired, instead of returning `login_wall: true` until someone re-uploads the profile. Needs `ai/interceptor/logins/<profile>.json` (checked in; bind-mounted read-only at INTERCEPTOR_LOGINS_DIR=/config/logins, re-read per request): {"allowed_origins": ["https://sso.enphaseenergy.com"], "values": {"username": "${ENV:INTERCEPTOR_LOGIN_ENPHASE_USERNAME}", "password": "${ENV:INTERCEPTOR_LOGIN_ENPHASE_PASSWORD}"}} — every value is an environment reference; the credentials themselves are set in .env and passed through the interceptor compose `environment:` block (an unset one is a 400 naming the variable). GET /profiles shows which reference names (`login_keys`) a profile has.

`login_actions` run ONLY if the tab lands on a URL matching `login_url_patterns`, once per capture, never retried (a wrong password can't lock the account by looping). Steps: wait_for / fill / click / press / select / wait — NO evaluate (422). `${key}` is resolved from the file's `values` ONLY in a fill `value` (`$$` = a literal $); a `${` in any other field is a 400. In the regular `actions`, `${…}` is plain text. Every fill first checks the tab's `location.origin` against the file's `allowed_origins` (again right before typing) and fails with `origin <o> not allowed for this fill` otherwise. The login steps use their own gate (real URL + document complete; login URLs allowed, no capture hook needed). When they finish, the session's usual wait sees the tab leave the login page and re-navigates to `url`; the serial-number `actions` (whose gate has been waiting out the login) then run as usual. `login_actions_timeout_seconds` (1-600, default 60) caps the login run; `capture_window_seconds` must cover the login, the SSO redirect and the target page load (~120 s). The login selectors were read off the live SSO form (sso.enphaseenergy.com/login: one page, #username, #password, input[type=submit].button "Log in"); a failed step's error names the one that missed if Enphase changes it.

The request (and so every log line, GET /jobs record and 422 echo) only ever carries `${password}`; the secret goes only into the in-memory steps handed to the browser. Response: the usual CaptureResponse plus `login_actions_report` — same shape as `actions_report`, steps named `login_actions[i]`, a fill reports {element, value_length} only; null unless login_actions were sent AND a login wall was hit (so null on the next run means the session the fast path persisted is still good). `login_wall` is true only if still on the login page at the end. The job log gets one line: `login_actions ok=<bool> failed_at=<index/type>`.

Errors (all before a port is taken): 400 no logins file for the profile, 400 unknown `${key}` (the message lists the defined names, never values), 400 `allowed_origins` missing/empty/not an origin, 400 `${` outside a fill value or a malformed reference, 400 `invalid login_actions: …` (e.g. unknown press key), 422 an `evaluate` step or a malformed step, 422 `login_actions` with empty `login_url_patterns`. See INTERCEPTOR.md § Login actions.

Navigate to `url` under the named profile, wait `wait_seconds` (1..600, default INTERCEPTOR_SCREENSHOT_WAIT_SECONDS=15 — Chrome spends the first ~4-5s booting and navigating, so values under ~8 mostly capture blank pages), then screenshot the page and quit. No XHR patterns. Internally a screenshot-only POST /capture, so port-pool slots, profile fast/slow path, GET /jobs visibility (phase capturing → screenshot → cleaning_up) and cancel all behave identically.

`format` jpeg (default, ~100-300 KB for a viewport) | png (lossless, often 1-3 MB) | webp. `quality` 1-100 applies to jpeg/webp only. `full_page: true` captures the whole scrollable document clamped to `max_height` CSS px (<= 16384, Chrome's limit) instead of the 1920x1080 headless viewport. `scale` (0 < s <= 2) multiplies the output — 0.5 roughly quarters the payload. `login_actions` / `login_actions_timeout_seconds` sign in automatically if the page redirects to a login wall — same semantics and errors as on POST /capture (see `POST /capture (login actions)`); `wait_seconds` must then cover the login, the redirect and the page load, and `login_actions_report` says what they did (null unless they ran).

Returns ScreenshotResponse: {job_id, url, status, login_wall, error, screenshot: {format, mime_type, width, height, full_page, bytes, page_url, data_base64} | null, screenshot_error, login_actions_report}. `status: 'loading'` is NORMAL for pages that fire no JSON XHRs (static pages) — it is the capture status, not the screenshot's; judge the shot by `screenshot` / `screenshot_error`. `page_url` is where the tab actually landed (redirects, login bounces). `width`/`height` are the requested clip x scale, not decoded from the image.

Errors: 400 bad profile name or invalid `login_url_pattern` regex, 429 port pool exhausted, 500 Chrome not found. A screenshot that fails AFTER navigation (e.g. Chrome crashed) is a 200 with `screenshot: null` + `screenshot_error` set. See INTERCEPTOR.md § Screenshots.

Snapshot of the port pool + all currently-running captures. Returns {max_concurrent, active_count, available, jobs: [JobBase, ...]} where each JobBase has {job_id, phase, created_at, updated_at, elapsed_seconds, metadata: {profile, url, port, used_base_profile, temp_dir, actions_done, actions_total}, result, error}. `phase` progresses `cloning` (slow path only) → `capturing` → `cleaning_up`; fast-path captures skip `cloning`. A capture with page_script/actions shows `actions` while they run (metadata.actions_done / actions_total count progress; both null otherwise), and one with a screenshot passes through `screenshot`.

Completed captures are NOT retained — they disappear the moment they return to their caller. Use this before firing /capture to see current load (avoid surprise 429s), or to correlate a `job_id` from a previous response. Mounted by common.jobs.router.build_router. See INTERCEPTOR.md § Observability.

Detail on one in-flight capture — same JobBase shape as an element of GET /jobs. Set the `jobId` collection variable to a 12-char hex id first.

Errors: 404 if the id isn't currently in flight. A 404 means either the id never existed OR the capture already finished — completed captures aren't retained (INTERCEPTOR.md § Limits: no completed-job history).

Signal an in-flight capture to wake early, quit Chrome, run cleanup, and return. Operator-only — deliberately NOT exposed on MCP (an LLM can't coordinate cross-agent cancellation). The `POST /capture` caller then receives a normal CaptureResponse with `status="cancelled"` plus any partial matches/captured_urls collected before the abort. Returns {job_id, cancelled: true, was_phase}.

Also the way to reclaim a hung `keep_open=true` slot — cancel bypasses the skip-cleanup path and always terminates Chrome + releases the port + drops the profile-lock (fast path) or temp dir (slow path).

Errors: 404 if the job is unknown or already completed, 409 if the job is already in `cleaning_up` phase (the finally block is running — too late to cancel). See INTERCEPTOR.md § Cancelling a stuck or long-running capture.

item.name: MCP
item.description:
FastMCP JSON-RPC over HTTP forwarded through the LiteLLM pass-through. Note that LiteLLM ALSO advertises the interceptor as an MCP server via `mcp_servers.interceptor` (url `http://interceptor:8080/mcp`) in litellm_config.yaml — models see the tools through that path, not this one. The requests below are useful for debugging the transport directly. Every MCP request MUST use trailing-slash (POST /mcp/), MUST send `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream`, and MUST start with an `initialize` call — copy the `mcp-session-id` response header into the `mcpSessionId` collection variable for subsequent calls.

Five tools are exposed: capture_url, screenshot_url, list_profiles, list_jobs, get_job. The `keep_open` and `debug_logging` knobs from POST /capture are deliberately omitted — both are operator-only debug flags. MCP tools NEVER raise — errors surface inside the payload (e.g. `status="error"` with an `error` field, or `{"error": "no active job ..."}`). capture_url and screenshot_url return a TextContent JSON block plus, when a screenshot was taken, an ImageContent block carrying the image itself (the JSON keeps only the metadata — no base64 duplicated into the text).

request.description: MCP handshake. Response headers include `mcp-session-id` — copy it into the `mcpSessionId` collection variable. Required before any tools/list or tools/call.
Enumerate available tools. interceptor exposes exactly five: capture_url, screenshot_url, list_profiles, list_jobs, get_job.

body.raw:
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 3,
  "method": "tools/call",
  "params": {
    "name": "capture_url",
    "arguments": {
      "url": "https://example.com/dashboard",
      "url_patterns": ["example\\.com/api/v1/items"],
      "profile": "{{profileName}}",
      "capture_window_seconds": 20,
      "login_timeout": 300,
      "max_matches_per_pattern": null,
      "screenshot": false,
      "screenshot_full_page": false,
      "screenshot_format": "jpeg",
      "screenshot_scale": 1.0,
      "page_script": null,
      "actions": null,
      "stop_when_matched": false,
      "login_url_patterns": null,
      "actions_ready_timeout_seconds": null,
      "login_actions": null
    }
  }
}

request.description: Model-invokable equivalent of POST /capture. Same core behavior. `keep_open` and `debug_logging` are NOT exposed here — operator-only. `screenshot: true` additionally captures the page at the end of the window: the result then carries an ImageContent block after the JSON text block, and the JSON's `screenshot` field holds {format, mime_type, width, height, full_page, bytes, page_url} (no base64). `screenshot_full_page`, `screenshot_format` (jpeg|png|webp) and `screenshot_scale` (0 < s <= 2) shape the image. `page_script` (JS expression run once the page is ready), `actions` (list of step objects — same shapes as on POST /capture (actions)) and `stop_when_matched` drive the page first; the JSON then carries `actions_report` and `ended_early`. HTTPException / validation failures (400 bad regex or bad action, 429 pool exhausted, 500 no browser, invalid scale, malformed action — the error names the field path, e.g. `actions.0.click.selector: Field required`) are wrapped into the return payload as `{status: "error", error: "...", matches: {p: [] for p in url_patterns}, captured_urls: [], screenshot: null, screenshot_error: null, actions_report: null, login_actions_report: null, ended_early: false}` rather than raised — the LLM can then read the error and retry. `login_url_patterns` (optional) replaces the default login-wall regexes (`login`, `signin`, `/auth`); pass the site's SSO host too when it doesn't match them (Enphase: `sso\.enphaseenergy\.com`), or an expired session reads as an empty result instead of `login_wall: true`. null keeps the defaults; [] disables detection. `actions_ready_timeout_seconds` (optional) bounds how long actions wait for the page to be ready; null = capture_window_seconds. `login_actions` (optional, list of step objects like `actions` minus `evaluate`) sign in only if the page hits a login wall, writing the credentials as references — e.g. [{"type": "fill", "selector": "input[type=email]", "value": "${username}"}, {"type": "fill", "selector": "input[type=password]", "value": "${password}"}, {"type": "click", "selector": "button[type=submit]"}] — resolved server-side from the profile's logins file (names in list_profiles' `login_keys`); the JSON then carries `login_actions_report`. The tool tells the model never to ask a user for real credentials. Same rules and errors as `POST /capture (login actions)`.

Model-invokable equivalent of POST /screenshot: navigate under the profile, wait `wait_seconds`, return an image of the rendered page. The result's `content` is [TextContent(JSON), ImageContent(image/<format>)] — the JSON carries {job_id, url, status, login_wall, error, screenshot: {format, mime_type, width, height, full_page, bytes, page_url}, screenshot_error, login_actions_report} and the image block carries the pixels, so a multimodal model can look at the page. `status: 'loading'` is normal for pages with no JSON XHRs. `page_url` shows where the tab actually ended up (login bounce etc.). Failures are returned in the payload (`status: 'error'` + `error`, or `screenshot: null` + `screenshot_error`), never raised. See INTERCEPTOR.md § Screenshots. `login_url_patterns` (optional) replaces the default login-wall regexes (`login`, `signin`, `/auth`); pass the site's SSO host too when it doesn't match them (Enphase: `sso\.enphaseenergy\.com`), or an expired session reads as an empty result instead of `login_wall: true`. null keeps the defaults; [] disables detection. `login_actions` (optional) — same as on capture_url: sign in on a login wall with `${username}` / `${password}` references, never real values.

Same shape as GET /profiles — {root, profiles: [{name, path, present, size_bytes, sentinel_present, login_keys, login_origins}, ...]}. `login_keys` are the `${…}` names a profile's login_actions may reference (never the values). Use before `capture_url` when the model doesn't already know which profile names exist. Only profiles with `sentinel_present: true` are usable headless — a `false` value means the profile hasn't been through the operator upload flow and Chrome would fall back to visible launch (which fails in the container with `Missing X server or $DISPLAY`).

Same shape as GET /jobs — {max_concurrent, active_count, available, jobs}. Use before firing `capture_url` to see how busy interceptor is (avoids surprise 429s when the pool is exhausted), or to correlate a job_id from a previous response with what's actually still running. Completed captures are NOT retained.

Same shape as GET /jobs/{job_id} for an in-flight capture — {job_id, phase, created_at, updated_at, elapsed_seconds, metadata, result, error}. If the id is unknown or the capture has already completed, returns `{"error": "no active job '<id>'"}` in the payload rather than raising (MCP tools never raise). Note the HTTP endpoint returns 404 in the same case — divergent from MCP by design.
